title: The Death of Hen variant

full_text:
A cock and a hen went up to the Nut Hill to gather hazelnuts, agreeing to share everything they found. But when the hen found a colossal nut, she swallowed it whole out of greed, and the giant shell lodged in her throat.

"Hurry, dear cock!" gasped the hen. "Run to the well and fetch water, or I will choke to death!"

The cock ran to the well, but the well demanded a wreath of silk from the bride. The bride demanded a garland of willow from the willow tree. The willow demanded a ribbon from the maiden. The cock ran frantically from one to another, fulfilling every demand with loyal devotion.

By the time he returned to the Nut Hill with the cool spring water, the hen had already choked and lay lifeless upon the grass.

Overcome by grief, the faithful cock built a funeral car, harnessed six mice, and conveyed the departed hen to her grave. A fox, a wolf, and a bear asked to ride along in mourning. But when the heavy car reached the rushing river, the bridge gave way, and the mourning party plunged into the deep stream, leaving the grieving cock to mourn his lost companion in lonely sorrow.
moral: Selfish disregard for warnings brings sorrow, while faithful comrades mourn together.
